in_greek.meaning: Γιος του Γούλφρικ, απελευθερωτής και ηγέτης, έτος ιερέων
in_greek.long_meaning: Γιος του Γούλφρικ, απελευθερωτής και ηγέτης, έτος ιερέων. Στην αρχαία Βρετανία, ο Γούλφρικ ήταν ηγεμόνας της Northumbria, ο οποίος προσπάθησε να δημιουργήσει ένα αχανές κράτος. Αυτό το όνομα είναι μια σύνθεση από τα γερμανικά και αγγλικά ονόματα, και έχει εκδοθεί σε διάφορα χριστιανικά ονόματα, όπως και το Γουίλιαμς.

in_latin.name: Williams
in_latin.meaning: filius Wulfrici, liberator et dux, annus sacerdotum
in_latin.long_meaning: Filii Wulfrici, liberator et dux, annus sacerdotum. In antiqua Britannia, Wulfricus fuit princeps Northumbriae, qui conatus est ut crearet imperium vastum. Nomen huius est compositum ex nominibus Germanicis et Anglicis, et est editum in diversos nomina Christiana, ut et Williams.

in_english.name: Williams
in_english.meaning: son of William, strong-willed warrior and leader, of noble birth
in_english.long_meaning: Son of William, strong-willed warrior and leader, of noble birth. The name William is derived from the Germanic words 'wil' meaning will or desire, and 'helm' meaning protection or defense. It is associated with the biblical figure of William, the son of the high priest, and has been borne by several saints, including Saint William of York and Saint William of Norwich. In modern times, the name has become popular due to its strong, masculine sound and its association with the name of the famous explorer William Shakespeare.

data.cultural_impact: The name Williams carried significant cultural impact, especially during the Middle Ages when it became a popular choice for Christian infants. Several influential figures and saints bore the name, leading to its widespread use and association with noble, strong, and protective figures. The name continues to be used and revered in the Western world.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Williams holds spiritual significance as it symbolizes a strong, unwavering will and protection from God. The name is derived from Old English 'will' meaning 'desire' or 'will' and 'helm' meaning 'helmet' or 'protector'. This name highlights the belief that having a strong desire and will can lead to protection and guidance from a higher power. The name Williams also pays homage to St. William of Vercelli and other devout saints named William, whose lives and teachings continue to inspire and influence Christians around the world.
